title: Should I Buy the Paint Myself or Let the Painter Supply It?
description: Buying your own paint can save a little on materials, but it often costs more in delays and wrong products, and with us it means no warranty. Here's how to decide, and what to ask your painter.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: for most homeowners, it's better to let the painting contractor supply the paint. Contractors usually pay trade pricing, know exactly how much to order, and pick the right product for each surface. At The Proud Paintbrush, our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty only applies when we supply the paint. Buying your own paint makes sense mainly when you already have a specific product you want and don't need a warranty on the job.

Reasons to Let Your Painter Supply the Paint

  • Price. Painting companies typically have contractor accounts at paint stores, often at better prices than retail. The savings from buying it yourself are usually smaller than people expect.

  • The right product for each surface. Walls, ceilings, trim, cabinets, bathrooms and exterior siding often need different products, primers and sheens. Picking the wrong one is the most common DIY-supply mistake.

  • The right amount. Running short mid-job means a store run and a possible color mismatch between batches. Buying too much leaves you with cans to store or dispose of.

  • Clear responsibility. If the paint fails, it's easier to sort out when one company chose and applied it. That's why we only warranty jobs where we supply the paint. Other contractors may limit or void their warranty when the homeowner buys it.

  • Less coordination for you. No hauling cans, no matching sheen names across brands, no guessing.

When Buying Your Own Paint Makes Sense

  • You have a specific brand and color already chosen and want to control the exact product

  • You already have unopened paint from the same batch, for example from a previous project or the builder

  • You're doing a very small job where convenience matters more than price and a warranty isn't important

If you go this route, tell your painter before the estimate. Confirm the product, sheen and quantity with them, and ask how it affects their warranty. With us, customer-supplied paint means the job isn't covered by our warranty.

What to Ask Your Painter About Paint

  • Which brand and product line will you use on each surface?

  • Is the paint cost included in the quote, and at what quality level?

  • Will you prime, and where?

  • Can I choose a different product, and how does that change the price?

  • Does the warranty cover materials, labor or both?

Product choice matters, but prep matters more. Read what matters more, paint brand or prep work for why.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it cheaper to buy your own paint for a painter?

Sometimes slightly, but often not. Contractor pricing, correct quantities and avoiding wrong products usually close the gap.

Does The Proud Paintbrush warranty jobs if I buy the paint?

No. Our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty covers jobs where we supply the paint, because we can only stand behind products we chose for the surface.

What paint does The Proud Paintbrush use?

We're a Sherwin-Williams paint partner and choose the product line for each surface and budget. We'll go over the options with you at the estimate.

Can I pick my own colors if the painter supplies the paint?

Yes. You choose the colors; the painter matches them in the right product and sheen. A color consultation can help if you're stuck.
